text.p: A German court on Thursday rejected a damages suit brought by tennis star Monica Seles against the German Tennis Federation (DTB) over security measures at a tournament where she was stabbed in 1993.
Lawyers for Seles had claimed 24.4 million marks ($15.75 million) for damages and lost earnings from her 27-month layoff after the attack at the Hamburg Open event.

The court rejected the U.S. star's claim that the players' bench in the stadium was too close to the spectators' stand, from where lathe operator Guenter Parche leapt to stab Seles in the back with a kitchen knife in April 1993.
It said Seles would have to pay the costs of the trial. The DTB welcomed the court's decision, saying it ensured direct contact between spectators and players at major events could be maintained.
Parche was given a two-year suspended sentence in October 1993 for grievous bodily harm. The trial judge ruled he was emotionally retarded and may not have been entirely responsible for his actions.

Prosecutors had asked the court to jail Parche for attempted murder. A subsequent appeal by Seles for a harder sentence failed. She told that hearing in a written statement the attack had "ruined her life".

Seles, suffering from fear and depression, postponed her comeback to the international tennis circuit several times and finally returned last year. But she has not taken part in any tournaments in Germany since her return.
Parche said at the time he wanted to wound Seles out of love for her German rival, Steffi Graf.
